1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' that introduces a time-clause pointing to a definite future event treated as certain. In oath and eschatological passages like this, it conveys 'at the time when / on the day when' — setting up a series of conditions whose answer (the main clause) comes later in the passage.
1.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of time — it has no case ending and never changes form. It governs the verb that follows (here a past-tense verb used for a future-certain event) and means 'when such-and-such happens'. It expects a later 'then…' clause to complete the thought.

2.meaning: The sun — the blazing celestial body. Here it is the subject of the opening sign of the Last Day.
2.grammar: A feminine noun made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject — the thing that performs/undergoes the verb that follows ('the sun … is wrapped up'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'sh', hence 'ash-shams'.

3.meaning: Is wrapped up / folded up and so extinguished — the sun's light is rolled together like a turban or a scroll and put out, its radiance gone.
3.grammar: A passive past-tense verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern, so the doubled middle letter signals a thorough, forceful wrapping-up. The vowelling 'u-i' (kuwwira) marks the passive: the sun is acted upon, not acting — 'it is wrapped up' (by Allah). The '-at' ending is third-person feminine singular ('she/it'), agreeing with 'the sun', which is feminine. Though grammatically past, it describes a future event rendered as certain.
3.root: ك-و-ر (k-w-r) — to wind/wrap round, coil up

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: The stars — the bright points of light scattered across the night sky. Here they are the subject of the second sign.
2.grammar: A plural noun made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject of the verb that follows ('the stars … fall'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n', hence 'an-nujūm'. Its singular is 'najm'.

3.meaning: Fall away losing their luster — the stars scatter, dim, and tumble down, their light extinguished and order broken.
3.grammar: An active past-tense verb in the reflexive/middle (Form VII) pattern, whose 'in-' prefix gives the sense of something happening to the subject itself — the stars 'become dimmed / fall of themselves'. The '-at' ending is third-person feminine singular, here agreeing with the (non-human) plural 'the stars', since Arabic treats non-human plurals as feminine singular. Though past in form, it depicts a certain future event.
3.root: ك-د-ر (k-d-r) — to be murky, dull, turbid (loss of brightness)

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: The mountains — the great masses of rock fixed in the earth. Here they are the subject of the third sign.
2.grammar: A plural noun made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject of the verb that follows ('the mountains … are set moving'). The 'l' of 'al-' is pronounced clearly here ('al-jibāl') because 'j' is a 'moon letter'. Its singular is 'jabal'.

3.meaning: Are set moving / made to pass away — the mountains, once immovable, are driven along and swept off, uprooted from their places.
3.grammar: A passive past-tense verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern; the doubled middle letter conveys causing thorough, repeated motion ('made to move along'). The 'u-i' vowelling (suyyira) marks the passive — the mountains are acted upon ('are moved away' by Allah). The '-at' ending is third-person feminine singular, agreeing with the non-human plural 'the mountains'. Past in form but future-certain in meaning.
3.root: س-ي-ر (s-y-r) — to travel, move along, journey

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: The full-term she-camels — pregnant camels in their tenth month, on the verge of delivering. Among the Arabs these were the most prized and cherished of possessions, so their being abandoned signals utter upheaval.
2.grammar: A plural noun made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject of the verb that follows ('the she-camels … are left untended'). The 'l' of 'al-' is pronounced clearly ('al-ʿishār') because 'ʿayn' is a 'moon letter'. Its singular is 'ʿusharāʾ'.
2.root: ع-ش-ر (ʿ-sh-r) — ten (linked to the tenth month of pregnancy)

3.meaning: Are left untended / neglected — the precious pregnant camels are abandoned with no one to herd or milk them, because on that Day every owner is too overwhelmed to care for what he once treasured.
3.grammar: A passive past-tense verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern; the doubled middle letter stresses a complete leaving-idle ('utterly neglected'). The 'u-i' vowelling (ʿuṭṭila) marks the passive — the camels are acted upon ('are left untended'). The '-at' ending is third-person feminine singular, agreeing with the non-human plural 'the she-camels'. Past in form, future-certain in sense.
3.root: ع-ط-ل (ʿ-ṭ-l) — to be unattended, idle, stripped/left without

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: The wild beasts — the untamed animals of the wilderness. Here they are the subject of the fifth sign.
2.grammar: A plural noun made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject of the verb that follows ('the wild beasts … are gathered'). The 'l' of 'al-' is pronounced clearly ('al-wuḥūsh') because 'w' is a 'moon letter'. Its singular is 'waḥsh'.

3.meaning: Are gathered together — the wild animals, normally scattered and fleeing one another, are herded and assembled in one place, all driven together in the terror of that Day.
3.grammar: A passive past-tense verb in the basic (Form I) pattern. The 'u-i' vowelling (ḥushira) marks the passive — the beasts are acted upon ('are gathered' by Allah), not gathering themselves. The '-at' ending is third-person feminine singular, agreeing with the non-human plural 'the wild beasts'. Past in form, but it describes a certain event of the Last Day.
3.root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r) — to gather/assemble, herd together (whence al-ḥashr, the Gathering)

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: The seas, oceans — large bodies of water. This is the plural form, 'the seas,' referring to all the great waters of the earth.

parts.en: nominative ending (marks the grammatical subject of the verb)

2.grammar: A plural noun (broken plural of baḥr). Like all broken plurals of inanimate things in Arabic, it is treated as grammatically feminine singular — which is why the following verb takes the feminine -at ending (sujjirat). The leading al- means 'the.' The final -u is the nominative case, marking 'the seas' as the grammatical subject. Since the verb is passive, the seas are the thing acted upon ('are set on fire / made to overflow'), not the doer.
2.root: ب-ح-ر (b-ḥ-r) — sea, vast expanse of water

3.meaning: They are set ablaze / made to boil over and overflow — the seas surge and burst their bounds, or are kindled into fire, as a sign of the world's undoing on the Last Day.

parts.en: was made to overflow / set on fire (intensive passive stem)

3.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern: 'they were made to overflow / set ablaze' — the doubled middle letter (sujjira, not sajara) signals an intensified, thorough action done TO the subject by an unnamed agent. The -at ending is feminine singular, agreeing with the grammatically feminine plural 'the seas.' Passive: the seas don't act; they are acted upon.
3.root: س-ج-ر (s-j-r) — to kindle/fill a fire; to make brim over

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: The souls — the inner selves or persons of human beings. This is the plural, 'the souls,' i.e. all people's selves.

parts.en: nominative ending (marks the grammatical subject of the verb)

2.grammar: A feminine plural noun (broken plural of nafs, 'soul/self'). The al- ('the') assimilates into the following n- (heard as an-nufūs). The final -u is the nominative case, marking 'the souls' as the grammatical subject. Because the verb (zuwwijat) is passive, the souls are paired by an unnamed agent — they are the ones acted upon, not the doers.
2.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath of life

3.meaning: They are joined in pairs / coupled — each soul is matched or reunited (commonly understood as souls rejoined to their bodies, or like joined with like), on the Day of Resurrection.
3.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern: 'they were paired up.' The doubled middle letter signals deliberate, thorough action done TO the subject. The -at ending is feminine singular, agreeing with the feminine plural 'the souls.' Passive: the souls are paired by an unnamed Doer (Allah), not by themselves.
3.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pair, mate, spouse, to couple together

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: The buried-alive baby girl — a female infant who, in pre-Islamic Arabia, was buried alive at birth. The word names the victim of that practice: 'the girl buried alive.'

parts.en: (one who is) buried alive — passive participle
feminine marker (the buried-alive female), with subject ending -u

2.grammar: A passive participle ('one who has been buried alive') made feminine by the -at ending (tāʾ marbūṭa), so it specifically names a girl. The final -u marks it as the subject of the next verb — 'the buried-alive girl' is the one who 'is asked.' Note: she is named as the subject, yet the question is really about her killers.
2.root: و-ء-د (w-ʾ-d) — to bury an infant alive

3.meaning: She is questioned / called to account — the buried infant is asked (about the wrong done to her), so that her killers stand exposed and answerable.
3.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (Form I): 'she was asked / questioned.' The vowel pattern su-i- marks the passive — the action is done TO her by an unnamed questioner (Allah). The -at ending is feminine singular, 'she,' agreeing with the buried baby girl.
3.root: س-ء-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, question, demand

1.meaning: For/by what…? — the start of the question put to (or about) her: 'for WHICH sin…?' It combines the preposition 'by/for/because of' with the question-word 'which / what.'

parts.en: for / because of / by reason of
genitive ending (required after the preposition bi-)

1.grammar: A preposition bi- ('for/because of') fused to the interrogative ayy ('which/what'). The final -i ending is genitive — the case forced by the preposition bi- — and it also links ayy to the following noun, giving 'for which [sin]…?' So the phrase opens a question: 'for what crime…?'

2.meaning: A sin, crime, offense — a punishable wrongdoing or fault for which one is blameworthy.

parts.en: genitive + indefinite ending ('a/some'), tied to the preceding 'which'

2.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -in (an 'n' sound, tanwīn) does two things at once: it marks the genitive case (because it follows 'for which…') and it makes the noun indefinite ('a sin / some sin'). The phrase reads 'for which sin…?'

3.meaning: She was killed / put to death — the completion of the question: for what sin was she (the baby girl) slain?
3.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (Form I): 'she was killed.' The vowel pattern qu-i- marks the passive — she did not act; she was slain by others. The -at ending is feminine singular, 'she,' agreeing with the buried baby girl. The whole clause: 'for what sin she was killed.'
3.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: The pages / scrolls / records — the written sheets on which each person's deeds are recorded. The plural means 'the pages' (of the deed-records).

parts.en: nominative ending (marks the grammatical subject of the verb)

2.grammar: A feminine plural noun (plural of ṣaḥīfa, 'sheet/scroll'). The al- ('the') assimilates into the following ṣ- (heard as aṣ-ṣuḥuf). The final -u is the nominative case, marking 'the pages' as the grammatical subject. Since the verb (nushirat) is passive, the pages are acted upon — 'are laid open / spread out' by an unnamed agent — not doers themselves.

3.meaning: They are spread open / unrolled / laid out — the deed-records are opened up and published for all to see, on the Day of Judgment.

parts.en: was spread open / unrolled (basic passive stem)

3.grammar: A past-tense passive verb (Form I): 'they were spread open.' The vowel pattern nu-i- marks the passive — the pages are unrolled by an unnamed Doer (Allah), they don't open themselves. The -at ending is feminine singular, agreeing with the feminine plural 'the pages.'
3.root: ن-ش-ر (n-sh-r) — to spread out, unfold, unroll, publish

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: The sky / heaven — the canopy above, the firmament. Here, 'the sky' as a single whole.

parts.en: nominative ending (marks the grammatical subject of the verb)

2.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The al- ('the') assimilates into the following s- (heard as as-samāʾ). The final -u is the nominative case, marking 'the sky' as the grammatical subject. Because the governing verb is passive, the sky is the thing acted upon — 'is stripped away / peeled off' by an unnamed agent — not the doer.
2.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness, that which is above

3.meaning: It is stripped off, peeled away, or flayed — like skin torn from a body or a covering ripped clean off. Describing the sky/heaven being torn away on the Day of Judgement.
3.grammar: Past-tense passive verb, feminine singular. The internal vowel pattern (u-i) makes it passive: the action is done TO the subject ('is stripped away'), not by it. The '-at' ending means a feminine 'it' did the receiving — here the sky (samā', feminine in Arabic).
3.root: ك-ش-ط (k-sh-ṭ) — to strip, peel, or flay off a covering

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: The Hellfire — specifically the blazing, intensely hot Fire of punishment. 'Al-Jaḥīm' carries the sense of a fiercely flaring, raging fire.
2.grammar: A definite noun. The final '-u' is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject of its clause — here the thing that 'is set ablaze.' The 'al-' makes it specific: THE Hellfire, not just any fire.
2.root: ج-ح-م (j-ḥ-m) — to blaze, to burn fiercely

3.meaning: It is set ablaze, kindled to a fierce blaze, or made to burn intensely. The doubled middle letter intensifies it: not merely lit, but stoked into a roaring fire.
3.grammar: Past-tense passive verb, feminine singular, in the intensive (doubled-letter, Form II) form. The doubling of the 'ʿ' adds force/repetition — 'fiercely set ablaze.' The u-i vowels make it passive ('is set ablaze'). The '-at' ending refers back to the feminine subject, al-Jaḥīm (the Hellfire).
3.root: س-ع-ر (s-ʿ-r) — to kindle, to set ablaze, to flare up

1.meaning: 'And when' — the connector 'and' joined to the time-word 'when', linking this sign to the previous one and continuing the list of events of the Last Day.
1.grammar: A joining word 'wa' ('and') prefixed to the indeclinable time-adverb 'idhā' ('when'). Neither part takes a case ending. Together they add another clause to the running series: 'and when … (happens)'.

2.meaning: Paradise — the Garden of eternal reward and bliss. 'Al-Jannah' literally means 'the Garden,' from a root meaning to cover or conceal, evoking dense, sheltering greenery.
2.grammar: A definite feminine noun, fully voweled 'al-jannatu' (note the doubled 'n', written with shaddah). The '-t-' marks it as feminine, and the final '-u' is the nominative ending, marking it as the subject — here the thing that 'is brought near.' The 'al-' makes it specific: THE Garden, Paradise.
2.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, or shroud (hence a 'garden' of covering foliage)

3.meaning: It is brought near, drawn close, or made to approach — Paradise being moved within sight and reach of the righteous on the Day of Judgement.
3.grammar: Past-tense passive verb, feminine singular, in the causative ('make/cause to') form. The u-i vowel pattern makes it passive: Paradise 'is brought near' by another (by Allah), it does not approach on its own. The '-at' ending refers to the feminine subject, al-Jannah (Paradise).
3.root: ز-ل-ف (z-l-f) — to draw near, to bring close

1.meaning: It knew / it comes to know — to have certain knowledge, to realize fully. Here: on that Day each soul will know with certainty what it has sent ahead.
1.grammar: Past-tense active verb, feminine singular ('it knew'). Though grammatically past, in this Judgement-Day passage it carries a future-certain sense ('will know') — the event is so sure it is spoken of as already done. The '-at' ending agrees with the feminine subject that follows, nafs ('soul').

2.meaning: A soul — the inner self, the person as a living, accountable being. Here indefinite: 'each / every soul,' every individual standing in judgement.
2.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun. The final '-un' (the 'nunation' double-u sound) is the nominative ending marking it as the subject ('a soul knew'), and being nunation rather than just '-u' it signals 'a soul / any soul' rather than a specific one.

3.meaning: What / that which — a connecting word introducing the thing known. Here it means 'what [deeds]' — the content of what each soul will know about its own actions.
3.grammar: A relative/interrogative particle meaning 'what' or 'that which.' It is invariable — it never changes its ending for case, gender, or number. Here it functions as the object of 'knew': the soul knows 'what it has brought.' The lengthened 'ā' is a recitation feature (it precedes a hamza in the next word).

4.meaning: It was made present / brought forward — what the soul has sent ahead and now finds set before it: its own deeds readied for the reckoning.

parts.en: passive prefix-vowel of the causative (Form IV) form
passive stem 'to be made present' (root ḥ-ḍ-r)

4.grammar: Past-tense passive verb, feminine singular, in the causative (Form IV) form — 'was made present, was brought forward.' The Form IV prefix is only the initial hamza + vowel (اُ); all three root letters ḥ-ḍ-r belong to the stem. The u-i vowel pattern marks it passive (the deeds are brought, they do not bring themselves), and the '-at' ending agrees with the feminine subject, the same nafs ('soul'): 'what was brought present for it.'
4.root: ح-ض-ر (ḥ-ḍ-r) — to be present, to attend (Form IV: to make/bring present)

1.meaning: But nay! / Indeed — an emphatic oath-opener. The 'lā' here does not negate; combined with 'fa-,' it grips the listener's attention and powerfully introduces the solemn oath that follows ('I do swear...').

parts.en: emphatic particle introducing an oath ('nay / indeed')

1.grammar: Two particles joined. 'Fa-' links to what came before; 'lā' before an oath is read by scholars not as a true 'no' but as an attention-seizing emphasis that strengthens the coming oath. Particles are invariable — no case endings. The lengthened 'ā' is a recitation feature before the next word's hamza.

2.meaning: I swear / I take an oath — a solemn first-person declaration affirming the truth of what follows by swearing upon Allah's creation.
2.grammar: Present-tense active verb, first-person singular ('I swear'). The 'u-' prefix means 'I,' and the final '-u' is the indicative ending, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact (not a command or wish). It declares an oath being made in the present moment.
2.root: ق-س-م (q-s-m) — to swear an oath; (also to divide/apportion)

3.meaning: By the ones that recede / retreat and hide — an oath sworn 'by the receding stars' (or planets) that slip back and vanish from sight, traditionally understood as the stars that disappear by day or the planets that retreat in their orbits.

parts.en: those that recede / withdraw and hide — with doubled 'n'

3.grammar: A preposition 'bi' (here 'by,' completing the oath) attached to a definite plural noun, fully voweled 'bil-khunnasi' (note the doubled 'n'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, required because the noun follows the preposition 'bi-' — together they mean 'by the receding ones.' 'Al-Khunnas' is a broken plural (jamʿ taksīr) on the فُعَّل (fuʿʿal) pattern of the active participle khānis ('one that recedes'); the doubled 'n' belongs to this plural pattern itself, not a verbal intensifier.
3.root: خ-ن-س (kh-n-s) — to recede, draw back, retreat and hide

1.meaning: Those that run their course and sweep along — the moving stars/planets that glide swiftly across the sky. The word names heavenly bodies that travel along their orbits.
1.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural on the pattern فَوَاعِل ('the running ones'), feminine in sense. It is a diptote: in the genitive its final consonant drops and it ends in '-i' rather than taking the usual two-vowel '-in'. It is genitive because it follows the oath particle 'by' carried over from the start of the passage ('by the running stars'). The genitive marks it as the object of that oath.

2.meaning: Those that disappear and hide themselves — describing the same stars as they set or vanish at daybreak, like a deer withdrawing into its lair. It pictures the heavenly bodies slipping out of sight.
2.grammar: A plural noun on an intensive pattern ('those that habitually hide/withdraw'), with a doubled (geminated) 'n' marked by the shadda — hence 'kunnas-', not 'kunas-'. It is a second noun coordinated with the previous one, a separate object of the same oath ('by the running ones, by the hiding ones'), not an adjective describing 'al-jawāri'. Its '-i' (genitive) ending matches 'al-jawāri' because both are governed by the oath 'by'.
2.root: ك-ن-س (k-n-s) — to sweep; to retreat into a covert/lair

1.meaning: And by the night — the period of darkness, here sworn upon as one of the signs of the Creator.
1.grammar: Noun with the definite article 'the'. The 'wa-' here functions as an oath particle, 'by', and the '-i' (genitive) ending is what it forces onto the noun it swears by ('by the night'). The ending therefore marks the object of the oath.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' that introduces a time-clause pointing to a definite future event treated as certain. In oath and eschatological passages like this, it conveys 'at the time when / on the day when' — setting up a series of conditions whose answer (the main clause) comes later in the passage.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of time — it has no case ending and never changes form. It governs the verb that follows (here a past-tense verb used for a future-certain event) and means 'when such-and-such happens'. It expects a later 'then…' clause to complete the thought.

3.meaning: It departed / drew on — describing the night as it advances into darkness or, conversely, retreats toward dawn. The word captures the night's coming or its withdrawing.

parts.en: it darkened / departed (3rd person masc. sing., past)

3.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular: 'it/he did'. The final fatḥa '-a' is the built-in ending for a completed action by a single masculine subject (here 'the night') and is part of the verb form itself, not a separate added piece. The reduplicated form (ʿas-ʿas) is an onomatopoeic verb suggesting a gradual onset or fading.
3.root: ع-س-ع-س (ʿ-s-ʿ-s) — quadriliteral reduplicated root: darkness of night, its coming on or departing

1.meaning: And by the dawn / morning — the first light of day, sworn upon as a sign.
1.grammar: Noun with the definite article 'the'. The 'wa-' is again the oath particle 'by', and the '-i' (genitive) ending marks the noun as the object sworn upon ('by the dawn').

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' that introduces a time-clause pointing to a definite future event treated as certain. In oath and eschatological passages like this, it conveys 'at the time when / on the day when' — setting up a series of conditions whose answer (the main clause) comes later in the passage.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of time — it has no case ending and never changes form. It governs the verb that follows (here a past-tense verb used for a future-certain event) and means 'when such-and-such happens'. It expects a later 'then…' clause to complete the thought.

3.meaning: It breathed / drew breath — a vivid image of the dawn as it 'breathes out' its light and spreads across the sky, as though the morning were inhaling and exhaling into life.

parts.en: it breathed/respired (3rd person masc. sing., past)

3.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular: 'it/he breathed'. The final fatḥa '-a' marks a completed action by a single masculine subject (here 'the dawn') and is built into the verb form itself, not a separately attached piece. The form (pattern tafaʿʿala) carries a sense of gradual, self-involved action — the dawn breathing itself open.
3.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — breath, soul, to breathe

1.meaning: Truly it / indeed it — an emphatic opener affirming with certainty that 'it' (the Qur'an) is what follows. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis (roughly 'most surely'), and the attached 'it' refers back to the revelation.
1.grammar: An emphasis particle 'inna' ('truly, most surely') with an attached pronoun 'it/he'. 'Inna' makes the noun or pronoun after it its subject (the اسم إنّ) in the accusative case; the suffix '-hu' is that subject pronoun, meaning 'it' (the Qur'an). It is a subject placed in the accusative by 'inna' — not a grammatical object. There is no tense here — it is a particle plus pronoun setting up an emphatic statement.

2.meaning: Is surely the speech / word of — affirming that the Qur'an is the very utterance conveyed by the noble messenger. The 'surely' adds emphatic confirmation.
2.grammar: An emphatic prefix 'la-' ('surely') attached to the noun 'speech'. The '-u' (nominative) ending marks this word as the predicate — what 'it' is being said to be ('it is surely the word…'). The 'la-' is the confirming 'lām' that often pairs with 'inna' for double emphasis. Being the first term of a possessive phrase ('word OF a messenger'), it keeps the nominative '-u'.

3.meaning: Of a messenger / an envoy — one who is sent to deliver a message; here the noble angelic messenger (Gabriel) who conveys the revelation.
3.grammar: An indefinite noun, 'a messenger'. The '-in' ending (a vowel '-i' plus nunation 'n') is both genitive and indefinite: genitive because it is the possessor in 'the word OF a messenger', and the final 'n' sound ('tanwīn') marks it as indefinite ('a', not 'the').
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message/messenger

4.meaning: Noble / honourable — generous, held in high honour and dignity; describing the messenger as exalted in rank and character.
4.grammar: An adjective, 'noble', describing 'a messenger'. Its '-in' ending (vowel '-i' plus nunation 'n') matches the noun it describes: genitive to agree with 'rasūlin', and indefinite ('a noble…') marked by the final 'n' sound. Adjectives in Arabic copy the case and definiteness of their noun.

1.meaning: Possessor of / endowed with — 'one who has' something. This word means 'owner/holder of' and links the messenger to a quality (here 'power'): 'possessed of power'.
1.grammar: A noun meaning 'owner/possessor of', which is always followed by what is owned. It appears here in the genitive form 'dhī' (ending in long '-ī'), agreeing with the messenger it further describes ('a messenger… possessed of power'). Its case is shown by the long '-ī' vowel rather than a short one. It cannot stand alone — it must be joined to a following noun.

2.meaning: Strength / power — might, force, capability; here the great power with which the angelic messenger is endowed.

parts.en: genitive + indefinite ending (the -t- is the feminine ending pronounced before -in)

2.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun, 'power'. It is the thing owned in 'possessor OF power', so it takes the genitive; the '-in' ending (vowel '-i' plus nunation 'n') is genitive and indefinite ('of power'). The feminine ending 'tā' is sounded as '-t-' here because a vowel follows it.

3.meaning: A spatial/relational word meaning 'in the presence of', 'near', or 'with'. Here it conveys nearness in honour and rank — the one described holds a position of closeness and standing 'in the presence of' the Lord of the Throne, not merely physical proximity.

parts.en: in the presence of / with / near

3.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of place (ẓarf makān). It is always followed by a noun in the genitive (here 'the Throne'), forming a possessive-type link: 'in the presence OF…'. The fixed -a ending is built-in to the word; it is not a working case-marker here. It functions as a frozen accusative used adverbially.
3.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, beside, or in the presence of

4.meaning: Possessor of / endowed with — 'one who has' something. This word means 'owner/holder of' and links the messenger to a quality (here 'power'): 'possessed of power'.
4.grammar: A noun meaning 'owner/possessor of', which is always followed by what is owned. It appears here in the genitive form 'dhī' (ending in long '-ī'), agreeing with the messenger it further describes ('a messenger… possessed of power'). Its case is shown by the long '-ī' vowel rather than a short one. It cannot stand alone — it must be joined to a following noun.

5.meaning: The Throne — the supreme Throne of Allah, the greatest of created things, symbolising His sovereignty, majesty, and dominion over all creation.
5.grammar: A definite singular noun. The -i ending is genitive: it is governed by the preceding adverb 'ʿinda' (in the presence of), so the two together mean 'in the presence OF the Throne'. The 'al-' marks it as 'the' (specific, well-known) Throne.
5.root: ع-ر-ش (ʿ-r-sh) — to build/roof; a throne, canopy, or elevated seat

6.meaning: Firmly established, secure, and held in high standing. Describes one whose position is solid and unshakeable — possessing rank, authority, and an honoured, well-fixed place.
6.grammar: An adjective in the pattern faʿīl, conveying a settled, intensive quality. The ending -in is genitive case plus tanwīn (nunation), the doubled 'n' sound marking it as indefinite. It is one of the attributes (naʿt) of the 'noble messenger' (the angel) mentioned earlier — that noun is genitive, so this adjective is genitive to match it. It describes the angel as firmly established, NOT the Throne.
6.root: م-ك-ن (m-k-n) — firmness, establishment, secure position and power

1.meaning: One who is obeyed — a figure of such authority that his commands are followed. Here it describes the noble angel (Gabriel) as being heeded and obeyed among the angels in the heavens.
1.grammar: A passive participle ('one who is obeyed', not 'one who obeys') from the hollow root ṭ-w-ʿ. The original form maṭwūʿ contracts to muṭāʿ because of the weak middle letter (wāw). It is another attribute (naʿt) of the same 'noble messenger', so it is genitive to agree with that earlier genitive noun. The -in ending is genitive plus nunation (indefinite, 'an obeyed one').

2.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'there' — pointing to a distant location, here 'there in the heavens', i.e. in the elevated realm where the angel is obeyed. (Note: the supplied gloss 'and' does not match this word; thamma means 'there', not the conjunction.)
2.grammar: An indeclinable demonstrative adverb of place ('there', referring to a far location). Its -a ending is a fixed, built-in vowel, not a case-marker — the word never changes form. It points to the place where the just-mentioned obedience occurs.
2.root: — (a frozen adverb; no triliteral verbal root)

3.meaning: Trustworthy and faithful — one who is entrusted and proves reliable, keeping safe whatever is committed to him. Describes the angel as a trusted bearer of the divine message.
3.grammar: An adjective in the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality ('thoroughly trustworthy'). It is the last in the series of attributes (makīn, muṭāʿ, amīn) all describing the same 'noble messenger' (the angel). Because that noun is genitive, each attribute — including this one — is genitive to match it. The -in ending is genitive plus nunation (indefinite, 'a trustworthy one').
3.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faithfulness

1.meaning: A two-part opener: 'and' joining to what precedes, plus a negating word 'not'. Together they introduce a denial — 'And… is not…'. The 'mā' here negates the statement that follows.
1.grammar: Two indeclinable particles. 'wa' is the connective 'and', linking this verse to the previous oath. 'mā' is a negating particle here meaning 'not', denying the predicate that comes after it ('your companion is NOT…'). Neither takes a case ending; their form is fixed.

2.meaning: Your companion — the one who keeps your company and is well-known to you. It refers to the Prophet Muḥammad (peace be upon him), whom his people knew intimately; 'companion' stresses that he was no stranger but their own familiar associate.
2.grammar: An active participle ('one who companions/accompanies') functioning as a noun, with the attached pronoun '-kum' meaning 'your' (referring to a group). The -u ending is nominative: it marks this word as the subject of the sentence — 'your companion' is the one about whom something is being denied.

3.meaning: Mad / possessed — driven out of one's senses, as if overcome by the jinn. The verse denies this of the Prophet: he is in no way insane or jinn-touched.
3.grammar: A passive participle ('one who is afflicted by jinn / made mad') preceded by the prefixed particle 'bi-'. This 'bi-' is an extra (redundant) particle added after the negation for emphasis — strengthening 'is NOT mad at all'. The 'bi-' forces the genitive case, hence the -in ending (genitive + indefinite nunation).
3.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover/conceal; from it 'jinn' and madness (the mind being veiled)

1.meaning: A three-part emphatic opener introducing a solemn, certain affirmation: 'and' + an oath-like emphasiser 'la-' ('most surely') + 'qad' (which, before a past verb, confirms that the action definitely happened). Together: 'And he most certainly did…'.
1.grammar: Three indeclinable particles, none taking a case ending. 'wa' connects to the previous verse; 'la-' is the emphatic 'surely', adding the force of an oath; 'qad' before a past-tense verb affirms the action truly and definitely occurred. Stacked, they make the following statement maximally certain.

2.meaning: He saw him — a completed act of seeing with the eyes. The subject is the Prophet, and 'him' is the angel (Gabriel), whom the Prophet genuinely beheld.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: the built-in subject is 'he' (the Prophet). The attached pronoun '-hu' is the object, 'him' (the angel). So the verb-form itself supplies 'he', and '-hu' supplies the one seen: 'he saw him'. Past tense marks the action as already accomplished.

3.meaning: On / at the horizon — the line where sky meets earth. Here it is the 'clear horizon' where the Prophet saw the angel; the phrase places the sighting at that bright, open edge of the sky.
3.grammar: A definite noun governed by the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('at/on/in'). Any noun after 'bi-' must be genitive, which is why it carries the -i ending. 'al-' makes it definite ('the horizon'). The whole phrase tells us where the seeing took place.
3.root: ء-ف-ق (ʾ-f-q) — horizon, the far edges/regions of the sky and earth

4.meaning: The clear, plain, evident one — that which makes things manifest and distinct. Here it describes the horizon as openly visible, but the root carries the active sense of 'making clear/manifest', so it means clear in itself and clarifying to the beholder.
4.grammar: An active participle (form IV, 'one that makes clear') functioning as an adjective, made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' ending is genitive, matching the noun it describes ('the clear horizon') because that whole phrase follows the preposition 'on'.
4.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, made manifest

1.meaning: A two-part opener: 'and' joining to what precedes, plus a negating word 'not'. Together they introduce a denial — 'And… is not…'. The 'mā' here negates the statement that follows.
1.grammar: Two indeclinable particles. 'wa' is the connective 'and', linking this verse to the previous oath. 'mā' is a negating particle here meaning 'not', denying the predicate that comes after it ('your companion is NOT…'). Neither takes a case ending; their form is fixed.

2.meaning: The detached pronoun 'he' — a standalone word for the third-person masculine singular subject. It often carries emphasis ('he himself') or acts as the subject of an equational sentence ('he is…').
2.grammar: A free-standing subject pronoun (not attached to any verb or noun). It is fixed in form and shows no case ending; the final '-a' is simply part of the built-in shape of the word, not a grammatical case marker.

3.meaning: The preposition 'on / upon / over'. It conveys being atop or above something, and by extension obligation or being 'against' someone, depending on context. Here it has the sense 'with regard to / concerning' the unseen.
3.grammar: A preposition, fixed in form. It puts the noun that follows it ('the unseen') into the genitive case. The word itself takes no case ending; its final long vowel is invariable.
3.root: — (preposition; relates to the notion of 'highness', ع-ل-و)

4.meaning: The unseen, the hidden realm — everything beyond the reach of human perception: that which is absent from the senses, including the future and the world of the divine that only Allah fully knows.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the unseen'). The final '-i' ending is genitive because the noun follows the preposition 'on/concerning' ('ʿalā'), which requires the genitive case.
4.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — to be hidden, absent, concealed from sight

5.meaning: One who is stingy, grudging, or withholding. Describing the Prophet, the verse denies this: he does not hoard or hold back the revelation of the unseen given to him, but conveys it fully and without grudging.
5.grammar: An intensive adjective of the 'faʿīl' pattern ('one who withholds'). The prefixed 'bi-' is an extra (emphatic) particle added after the negation — 'he is not in the least a withholder' — and it forces the genitive '-in' ending; the doubled '-n' (nunation) shows the word is indefinite ('a withholder'). Though 'bi-' is a preposition in form, here it adds emphasis rather than the literal sense 'with'.
5.root: ض-ن-ن (ḍ-n-n) — to be miserly, to withhold grudgingly

1.meaning: A two-part opener: 'and' joining to what precedes, plus a negating word 'not'. Together they introduce a denial — 'And… is not…'. The 'mā' here negates the statement that follows.
1.grammar: Two indeclinable particles. 'wa' is the connective 'and', linking this verse to the previous oath. 'mā' is a negating particle here meaning 'not', denying the predicate that comes after it ('your companion is NOT…'). Neither takes a case ending; their form is fixed.

2.meaning: The detached pronoun 'he' — a standalone word for the third-person masculine singular subject. It often carries emphasis ('he himself') or acts as the subject of an equational sentence ('he is…').
2.grammar: A free-standing subject pronoun (not attached to any verb or noun). It is fixed in form and shows no case ending; the final '-a' is simply part of the built-in shape of the word, not a grammatical case marker.

3.meaning: 'The word / speech / saying of…'. Here 'qawl' means an utterance or pronouncement, and the phrase asserts what the Qur'an is NOT — namely, the speech of a devil.
3.grammar: A noun ('speech') prefixed with 'bi-', which here is an extra (emphatic) particle after the negation — 'it is not in the least the speech of…'. The '-i' ending is genitive (governed by 'bi-'). The word also stands at the head of a possessive chain — 'the speech OF a devil' — with the next word in the genitive.
3.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

4.meaning: A shaytan — a devil or satan: a rebellious, malevolent being (whether from the jinn or among humans) that is far from goodness and given to leading astray. The term denotes an evil, cast-off spirit.
4.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a devil'). The genitive '-in' ending (with nunation, the doubled '-n') marks it as the possessor in the chain 'the speech OF a devil'. The nunation also shows it is indefinite ('a devil', not 'the devil').
4.root: Disputed: many lexicographers take it as triliteral ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n, 'to be remote from mercy/good'), treating the yā' as an added letter; others treat it as quadriliteral ش-ي-ط-ن with the yā' as a fourth root letter.

5.meaning: Accursed, driven away, pelted — one who is stoned and expelled from divine mercy. It is the standard epithet of Satan, picturing him as cast out and rejected.
5.grammar: An adjective of the 'faʿīl' pattern carrying a passive sense ('one who is stoned/driven away'). It describes 'devil', so it matches that noun by also being indefinite and genitive — shown by the '-in' ending (nunation). The doubled 'r' at the start reflects assimilation of the preceding word's '-n' into this 'r' when read aloud.
5.root: ر-ج-م (r-j-m) — to stone, pelt; to drive away, curse

1.meaning: 'So where…?' — an interrogative meaning 'to where / in what direction', here used as a rhetorical rebuke: 'so where then are you going (with your denial)?', implying there is no valid path away from this truth.
1.grammar: A connective prefix 'fa-' ('so/then') joined to the question-word 'ayna' ('where'). 'Ayna' is fixed in form and takes no case; its final '-a' is part of its built-in shape, not a case ending. It asks about destination or direction.

2.meaning: 'You (all) are going / heading off / departing'. The verb pictures setting out toward something; in context, 'where are you going?' rebukes the deniers for the direction their thinking takes them.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix signals a 'you' subject, and the '-ūna' ending makes it masculine plural ('you all go'). The final '-na' marks the indicative mood — i.e. a plain statement/question ('you are going'), as opposed to a command or a subjunctive 'that you go'.
2.root: ذ-ه-ب (dh-h-b) — to go, depart, set off

1.meaning: The negating particle 'in' meaning 'not'. Paired with 'illā' ('except') that follows, it forms the restrictive frame 'it is nothing but… / only…', strongly limiting the statement to what comes after 'except'.
1.grammar: A particle of negation ('not'), fixed in form with no case ending. Here it is the negative half of the 'in… illā' construction ('it is not… except…'), which together means 'it is only…'. It governs nothing grammatically by way of endings.

2.meaning: The detached pronoun 'he' — a standalone word for the third-person masculine singular subject. It often carries emphasis ('he himself') or acts as the subject of an equational sentence ('he is…').
2.grammar: A free-standing subject pronoun (not attached to any verb or noun). It is fixed in form and shows no case ending; the final '-a' is simply part of the built-in shape of the word, not a grammatical case marker.

3.meaning: 'Except / but / only'. A particle of exception that, after a negation, carves out the sole thing affirmed: 'nothing but…'. With the preceding 'in' it yields 'this is only a reminder…'.
3.grammar: An exceptive particle, fixed in form with no case ending. Following the negation 'in' ('not'), it restricts the meaning to what comes next, giving the sense 'nothing/none except…' i.e. 'only'. It is treated as a single, unanalyzable particle (it is not built from smaller meaningful pieces in the word's actual structure).
3.root: — (particle, no root)

4.meaning: A reminder, an admonition, or a call to remembrance — something that brings a truth back to mind. The Qur'an is described as 'a reminder,' awakening people to what they already know deep down. The indefinite '-un' ending ('a reminder') stresses how complete and significant it is.
4.grammar: A masculine singular noun, indefinite. The final '-un' (the two-dot tanwīn) does two things at once: the 'u' marks the nominative case (it is the subject/predicate of the sentence — 'it is a reminder'), and the added 'n' sound makes it indefinite, i.e. 'a reminder' rather than 'the reminder.'
4.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to call to mind

5.meaning: To the worlds, to all created realms and peoples — every nation and age of mankind (and by extension all conscious beings). The phrase frames the Qur'an as a universal reminder, not limited to one community or time.
5.grammar: A masculine plural noun preceded by the preposition 'li-' ('to/for'); the 'l-' is the definite article 'the.' Because it follows a preposition, the noun is in the genitive (object-of-preposition) case, and the sound-masculine-plural genitive ending is '-īna' — so 'ʿālam' (world) becomes 'ʿālamīna' ('the worlds') governed by 'to.' (The doubling of the 'l' in 'lil' is just the article's 'l' assimilating after 'li-'.)
5.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; 'ʿālam' (a world) is that by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: For whoever, for the one who — introduces the person to whom the reminder applies: 'for whoever among you wills…'. It combines the preposition 'for/to' with the relative/conditional pronoun 'whoever.'
1.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to the pronoun 'man' ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people. The full form is 'liman.' 'man' is built on a fixed shape and never changes for case: the mīm simply carries a short 'a' (fatḥa) and the final nūn is silent (sukūn) — there is no tanwīn and no case ending at all. It serves as the object of 'for' and opens a relative/conditional clause ('for whoever wills…').

2.meaning: He willed, he wished, he chose — to want or intend something and set it in motion. Here it describes the person who 'wills' to walk the straight path; the act of willing is presented as a real choice given to the human being.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular: 'he willed' (full form 'shāʾa'). The final '-a' (fatḥah) is the standard ending of this 'he did' form. Although the action is grammatically 'past,' after the relative 'man' ('whoever') it carries a general, timeless sense — 'whoever wills.' The long 'ā' comes from a weak middle-root letter, and the word ends in a hamza (ʾ).
2.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to want

3.meaning: Among you, from among you (plural) — specifying a group out of a larger whole: 'whoever of you.' It addresses the listeners directly as 'you all.'
3.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from/among/of') with the attached pronoun '-kum' meaning 'you' for a group of (typically male or mixed) people. Attached pronouns after a preposition do not change form for case, so '-kum' is fixed; together they mean 'from among you all.'
3.root: — (preposition + pronoun; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: That, to — a connector that turns the following verb into a goal or content clause, like English 'to (do)' or 'that (he) should.' Here: 'wills … to take the straight way.' It points forward to an intended action.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle ('an' meaning 'that/to') that introduces a verb and puts it into the subjunctive mood — signalling an aim or intended action rather than a stated fact. It has no case ending of its own; its job is to govern the verb that follows (here making 'he takes a straight way' mean 'to take a straight way').

5.meaning: He goes straight, he keeps to a straight course, he stays upright and steadfast — to follow the straight path consistently and remain firm upon it. It conveys not just starting on the right road but holding steadily to it.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he…'), in the derived 'istafʿala' pattern (a form that often means to seek or hold to something — here 'to seek/keep straightness'). The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he.' Crucially, the final vowel is '-a' (fatḥah), not the usual '-u': this is the subjunctive triggered by 'an' before it, so the sense is 'to go straight / that he should go straight.'
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; the derived form means to be straight, upright, steadfast

1.meaning: A two-part opener: 'and' joining to what precedes, plus a negating word 'not'. Together they introduce a denial — 'And… is not…'. The 'mā' here negates the statement that follows.
1.grammar: Two indeclinable particles. 'wa' is the connective 'and', linking this verse to the previous oath. 'mā' is a negating particle here meaning 'not', denying the predicate that comes after it ('your companion is NOT…'). Neither takes a case ending; their form is fixed.

2.meaning: You (all) will, you wish, you want — the act of willing or choosing, addressed to a group: 'you cannot will (it) except…'. It places human willing in view before subordinating it to Allah's will.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, second person masculine plural — full form 'tashāʾūna' ('you all will'), with a hamza (ʾ) between the long ā and the wāw. The 'ta-' prefix marks 'you,' and the ending '-ūna' marks both the plural 'you all' and the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact). The intact '-na' shows the verb is not cut down by any subjunctive or jussive particle here.
2.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to want

3.meaning: 'Except / but / only'. A particle of exception that, after a negation, carves out the sole thing affirmed: 'nothing but…'. With the preceding 'in' it yields 'this is only a reminder…'.
3.grammar: An exceptive particle, fixed in form with no case ending. Following the negation 'in' ('not'), it restricts the meaning to what comes next, giving the sense 'nothing/none except…' i.e. 'only'. It is treated as a single, unanalyzable particle (it is not built from smaller meaningful pieces in the word's actual structure).
3.root: — (particle, no root)

4.meaning: That, to — a connector that turns the following verb into a goal or content clause, like English 'to (do)' or 'that (he) should.' Here: 'wills … to take the straight way.' It points forward to an intended action.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle ('an' meaning 'that/to') that introduces a verb and puts it into the subjunctive mood — signalling an aim or intended action rather than a stated fact. It has no case ending of its own; its job is to govern the verb that follows (here making 'he takes a straight way' mean 'to take a straight way').

5.meaning: He wills, He wishes — used here of Allah: 'unless Allah wills.' It expresses the divine will, the decisive willing upon which everything ultimately depends.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular — full form 'yashāʾa' ('He wills'), ending in a hamza (ʾ) followed by the case vowel. The 'ya-' prefix marks the subject (here Allah). The final vowel is '-a' (fatḥah) rather than '-u' because it follows the particle 'an' ('that/unless'), which puts the verb in the subjunctive — hence 'unless He wills / that He should will.' The long 'ā' is from the weak middle-root letter.
5.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to want

6.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God, the sole Creator and Sustainer worshipped in Islam. It is a unique name, not a common noun, and has no plural or gender.
6.grammar: The proper name 'Allah,' here ending in '-u' (ḍammah), which marks the nominative case: it is the subject of the verb — 'unless Allah wills.' In connected speech after the preceding word the form reads 'l-lāhu,' where the 'ā' stays long (اللّٰهُ). The name is treated as fully definite in itself, so it takes a single short vowel ('-u') with no indefinite 'n' sound.
6.root: — (the proper divine name; not derived from a triliteral root in the ordinary sense)

7.meaning: Lord, Master — the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs all that He has created, bringing it from stage to stage to its completion. 'Rabb' blends ownership, lordship, and loving upbringing; no single English word captures it, hence 'Lord' as a near-equivalent.
7.grammar: A masculine singular noun, definite by being the first term of a possessive phrase ('Lord OF the worlds'). The final '-u' (ḍammah) marks the nominative case — it stands in apposition to 'Allah' (Allah, the Lord of all worlds). Because it is the possessed term leading into 'the worlds,' it takes a plain '-u' with no indefinite 'n.'
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, own, and master

8.meaning: Of the worlds, of all created realms and peoples — every nation, age, and order of creation. Joined to 'Lord,' it gives 'Lord of all the worlds,' affirming Allah's universal lordship over everything that exists.
8.grammar: A definite masculine plural noun ('the worlds') functioning as the possessor in 'Lord of the worlds.' The sound-masculine-plural ending '-īna' here is genitive, because it is the second term of a possessive phrase ('Lord OF the worlds') — that is what links it to 'Lord' before it. The 'l-' is the definite article 'the.'
8.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'ʿālam' (world) is that through which the Creator is known
